questions.question: What does 'negative wrap-around' specifically handle?
options: Shifting past Z going forward
Shifting backward past A, wrapping around to continue from Z
Only applies to number coding
A rule with no practical use
questions.rationale: Negative wrap-around specifically covers the case of shifting backward past A, which wraps around to continue counting down from Z.

questions.question: What is 'letter-to-number coding'?
options: Converting numbers into letters
Replacing each letter with its alphabet position (or a value derived from it) as a number
A rule that ignores numbers entirely
Only used for vowels
questions.rationale: Letter-to-number coding replaces each letter with a numeric value, typically its alphabet position or something derived from it.

questions.question: What does 'sum coding' typically compute for a word?
options: The word's letter count only
The total sum of all its letters' alphabet positions
The product of all its letters' positions
The difference between its first and last letters
questions.rationale: Sum coding adds together the alphabet-position values of every letter in the word to produce a single numeric code.

questions.question: What does 'product coding' compute, in contrast to sum coding?
options: The same total as sum coding
The product (multiplication) of all the letters' alphabet positions, instead of their sum
Only the first letter's position
The word's length
questions.rationale: Instead of adding the position values together, product coding multiplies them all together to produce the code.

questions.question: What does 'difference coding' typically compute?
options: The sum of all letters' positions
The difference between the positions of two specific letters (often the first and last)
The product of two letters' positions
The total number of letters
questions.rationale: Difference coding typically computes the numeric gap between two specific letters' positions, commonly the first and last letters of the word.

questions.question: What does 'average coding' compute for a word?
options: The sum of its letters' positions
The average (mean) of all its letters' alphabet positions
Only the middle letter's position
The word's total letter count
questions.rationale: Average coding computes the mean of all the letters' alphabet-position values, dividing their sum by the number of letters.

questions.question: What does 'sum of odd/even positions' refer to?
options: Summing only the first and last letters
Separately summing the alphabet-position values of letters sitting at odd-numbered spots in the word versus even-numbered spots
A rule with no real distinction
Summing only vowels
questions.rationale: This coding separately totals the position values of letters occupying odd word-positions (1st, 3rd, 5th...) versus even word-positions (2nd, 4th, 6th...).

questions.question: What is 'vowel-consonant coding'?
options: A rule that ignores vowels entirely
A rule that treats vowels and consonants differently, such as applying a different transformation to each group
A rule that only applies to consonants
A rule identical to letter-shift coding
questions.rationale: Vowel-consonant coding applies different transformation rules depending on whether each letter is a vowel or a consonant.

questions.question: What does 'letter type coding' generally classify letters by?
options: Their physical appearance
A property such as vowel/consonant, or other categorical groupings, which determines how each letter is transformed
Their frequency in the dictionary
Their color, if written in color
questions.rationale: Letter type coding classifies each letter by some categorical property (like vowel vs consonant), and that classification determines the transformation applied to it.
